hero.headline:
Perfect Photo,
Perfect Grip
hero.subtext: On‑device AI measures hand size via A4 reference, recommends your optimal grip, and tracks your next string‑job.

howItWorks.heading: From photo to recommendation in under 30 seconds.
howItWorks.step1Body: Lay an A4 sheet flat on the table with your palm resting on it.
howItWorks.step2Body: Hold at least 50 cm above, keep your palm open, fingers and heel fully in frame.
howItWorks.step3Body: AI returns the recommended size and adjacent sizes. You can fine-tune manually.

features.heading: What it does for you.
features.subheading: Six tools. One download. Works fully offline.
features.item1Body: On-device inference. The photo is discarded right after processing. Nothing is uploaded.
features.item2Body: Enter palm length and ring finger length to get a recommended size and wrap-driven size shift.
features.item3Body: Default restring cycles per material (polyester / multifilament / natural gut). Local notifications when due.
features.item4Body: Convert main to cross tension, get a main-cross delta, quick refs for 16x19 and 18x20 patterns.
features.item5Body: Log multiple rackets with specs and notes. Stored locally, backup whenever you want.
features.item6Body: Informational cards on TFCC and tennis elbow. Not medical advice. See a doctor if pain persists.

privacyStrip.heading: Your photos stay on your phone.
privacyStrip.body: AI measurement runs entirely on-device. Once your photo is processed, we neither store nor upload it.

faq.heading: Common questions.
faq.q1: How accurate is the AI measurement?
faq.a1: We return a recommended size plus or minus one adjacent size with a confidence hint. Geometric error between your palm plane and the A4 sheet is a known physical limit. We do not claim millimeter precision and we do not fabricate percentage numbers.
faq.q2: Do I have to use A4 paper?
faq.a2: We strongly recommend it. A4 is a reference of known size used to convert pixels into millimeters. Other sheet sizes or objects work too, as long as you know their real dimensions when taking the photo.
faq.q3: What if my photo is taken at an angle?
faq.a3: Try to shoot straight down. If the angle is off, the confidence drops to medium or low and the result may drift by one or two grip sizes. Recompute with a flatter photo in that case.
faq.q4: Can I skip the camera and measure manually?
faq.a4: Yes. The manual entry lets you type palm length and ring finger length without invoking the camera. The two flows coexist and you can switch at any time.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.section1Body: AceCrush Craft V1.0 runs locally. All grip size data, racket archives, and restring logs are stored in your device's local database (SQLite) and are not sent to any server. The app has no account system and does not collect your name, email, phone number, or other identity information.
privacy.section2Body: When you actively use AI grip size measurement, the app will request camera access. The photo is processed only on-device (MediaPipe HandLandmarker or server-side OpenCV plus MediaPipe), then immediately discarded. It is not saved to your photo library and not uploaded to any cloud.
privacy.section3Camera: Camera (android.permission.CAMERA): used only on the AI measurement screen. Revoke by toggling it off.
privacy.section3Notification: Notifications (android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS): used only for restring expiry reminders. Disable in system settings.
privacy.section4Body: This app uses open source components: Flutter, drift, flutter_local_notifications, url_launcher, opencv_dart, and MediaPipe Tasks Vision. None of them actively collect personal information.
privacy.section5Body: If on-device AI inference fails (low-end hardware or iOS-side on-device CV not yet shipped), the app may send a single photo to our independently deployed CV service (port 8081). The service processes the image and discards it immediately. Only metadata such as device ID, SHA256, byte size, latency, and confidence is logged for quality improvement. The original image is not retained.
privacy.section6Body: Policy updates ship with new app releases and are reflected both in the in-app Settings - Privacy policy screen and on this page. Questions: hi@acecrush.dev.
